rationale.conceptual: The work uses established methods (DFT with van der Waals correction, MD with specific force fields) but their correct application requires domain knowledge in computational chemistry/materials science: selecting pseudopotentials, convergence, NPT ensemble protocols, virial stress, and post-processing. Not trivial, but no novel algorithm derivation.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has 7+ distinct stages (DFT relaxation, adsorption energy calculation, MD model building, NPT equilibration, tensile test, shear test, roughness computation) with dependencies; must orchestrate two different simulation codes (Quantum ESPRESSO/LAMMPS), handle equilibration (3 ns) and production runs, and average multiple shear runs. Fragile multi-tool orchestration with non-trivial I/O.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires reproducing DFT adsorption energies and MD stress-strain curves using standard but non-trivial methods in computational materials science. Conceptual difficulty is moderate (understanding DFT-D2, PCFF/AIREBO, equilibration protocols). Execution is complex: multi-stage pipeline with DFT relaxation, MD model construction, NPT equilibration, uniaxial tension, longitudinal shear, and roughness analysis, involving multiple tool invocations and data orchestration.

compute_estimate.reasoning: DFT supercells of ~32 atoms, MD systems of a few thousand atoms; simulation lengths of 3 ns (MD) and moderate strain tests. Memory footprint is moderate; no large datasets; all inputs generated computationally.
